label: Explained absence: an admitted reason versus positive fixing
term: Explained absence: an admitted reason versus positive fixing
resolution: An absence at a root is 'explained' in sense 1 when some fact is admitted as a reason for the lack fact in the #755 arena (ADMITTED_EXPLICABILITY_ROLE_1, the sense of every PSR and inquiry bridge in the graph), and in sense 2 when it is positively fixed: the admissibility constraints or a carried exclusion settle it. 'No unexplained absence at roots' (9281317d, with the definition a5452da9) denies an absence that sense 2's first disjunct leaves open; under the necessity direction of member grounding that is the denial of sense 2. Sense 1 does not give sense 2: a bare negative clause, or any necessary truth under necessaryReasons, is an admitted reason for a necessary lack that no admissibility constraint fixes (InquiryClosure rival row). Passing from sense 1 to sense 2 is the explicit open bridge 'an absence of an actual root with an admitted reason is positively fixed' (RootLackReasonsPositive), listed in sense_bridges, or the composition of the reason-essence thesis, carriage and member grounding (factorization in the InquiryClosure results). See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section on inquiry and closure at the root.
